- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of forecast horizon).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or overshoot after sharp price spikes in history.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, suggesting mean reversion or lagged adjustment.
- When history shows strong downward momentum, model fails to reflect it, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Forecasts show high variance but lack sensitivity to recent low-price trends; should adjust downward when recent 7–14 day average is below 70% of historical mean.
- Avoid over-reliance on recent high peaks; apply smoothing or decay weighting to recent values to reduce overshoot bias.
- If true outcome is below 65% of historical 30-day average, reduce forecast by 5–10% to account for mean reversion.
- When model forecast exceeds true outcome by >10% for 3 consecutive days, apply downward correction of 2–5% per day to avoid overcorrection lag.
